utpāta
(‘reversal of natural order’)
------------------------------------------
Belief in certain unnatural occurrences presaging future events is common to mankind since the ancient days. Such occurrences are called adbhuta or निमित्त or उत्पात. The words adbhuta and उत्पात are used as synonyms. उत्पात always indicates the evil happenings.
The epics and the पुराणस् are full of descriptions of these utpātas. Their effects can, generally speaking, be offset or reduced by the performance of शान्तिस्. (See ŚĀNTIS for details.)
The utpātas are divided into three classes: दिव्य (arising from heavenly sources); āntarikṣa (springing from the atmospheric region); bhauma (appearing on the earth).
Divya is indicated by the abnormal condition of the प्लनेत्स् and the स्तर्स्, like eclipses and appearance of comets. Āntarikṣa utpātas are hurricanes, unusual clouds, fall of meteors, abnormal reddish appearances of the quarters and strange rainfall (like bloodred water). Bhauma utpātas are earthquakes and unusual states of water reservoirs.
A few of the utpātas mentioned in the epics and the पुराणस् may now be set out here:
Terrible द्रेअम्स्; constant howling of jackals; solar एच्लिप्से at an unusual time; flashes of lightnings without clouds; carnivorous birds like vultures sitting on temples, fort-walls and bastions; spontaneous fires; haloes round the sun and the मोओन्; rain of mud or blood-red water; images of gods trembling, dancing, laughing or weeping; strange births as of an ass from a cow and so on.
When such utpātas occur, it is the duty of the king to get the appropriate शान्तिस् performed.
